correctness.rationale: Weighted matrix-tree/Cauchy--Binet computes the unnormalized Walsh coefficient as n^{-1} times the product of n-2 times Laplacian eigenvalues over constants orthogonal complement. An incidence Gram matrix gives lambda_max <= |S|+1; equality iff S is a star, with the triangle exception checked. At n=2m this yields strict positive W for |S|<=m-2, exact star-only zeros at m-1, and a negative star at m. For odd n all W are odd by Cayley n^{n-2}. Independent integer Prüfer/Walsh and determinant checks from verify_cayley.py passed at the stated finite orders. No finite experiment is used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The all-order result determines a sharp growing degree boundary for lost Fourier information under counting convolution by a canonical graph-basis family. It distinguishes odd-order full recovery from even-order first losses, completely classifies and counts the first lost edge-frequency modes, and locates the first attainable negative multiplier. This natural low-degree invariant is useful without an exhaustive full Fourier nullity. Its all-parameter star equality class is more than a textbook Cayley count or a parameter renaming.
